item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
It's attached to SCP-023's article for purely out-of-universe reasons (to encourage WikiWalking); in-universe, the Foundation doesn't know any of this, and has no good way of finding it out without resorting to my least-favourite explanation convention: The anonymous note at the end. This dilemma bugged me for years until I decided to just write a tale instead.

I'll try to keep this character in mind for later things, but she's fairly limited in her scope of unique ways to affect a story that's mostly about physical things.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I really enjoy myself some metaphors and symbolism, but I felt myself doubting whether things were metaphorical, what the metaphor was, or if they were just other Skippy-type things. Thanks to Pig_catapult that was all cleared up, but I still have a couple doubts. I caught that “my-children-who-birthed-me” was humanity, but I didn’t know what part of it or who “me” is. The Black Plague was picked up by me too, and it was probably the clearest metaphor, at least to someone who knows anything about medieval Europe. I suspected the narrator to be 023, but the end disproved that, leaving me wondering about the narrator (which I would LOVE to read more about, by the way). I think there should be more reason why this was attached to 023’s profile, maybe just something that said it was a note from somewhere?
You’ve really got this going in an interesting direction and I’d want it to keep going, but there are some p(l)otholes in the road. I like the mystery element, but either there’s still something critical left out or if I just don’t understand.
TL;DR I want more story because I look forward to its progression but also because I am confusion?¿?

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Because I wanted to get the story I couldn't tell with the SCP-023 article itself out in the 'verse instead of relegating hints of it to the discussion page and The Leak.

[Minor spoilers]
– hide block

While worded poetically, "the passions of the dead" is still a literal description.
"My-children-who-birthed-me" is half metaphorical and half literal.
"The light that brings life" is literally just the sun.
The title is a hint about the narrator, and the apostrophe placement was very deliberate.

[Major spoilers]
– hide block

The narrator and SCP-023 are both abstract entities born from the emotions of dying humans. The more people die feeling a given emotion, the more "vast" the corresponding abstract entity. The narrator embodies protective maternal love, and cannot help but regard humanity as her children even though she's aware the relationship is factually reversed. SCP-023, on the other hand, was born during the Black Death, and when people are dying of plague faster than you can dig graves, sometimes you just gotta throw the corpses into a big pit and set it on fire.
